d: Northern navigational constellation containing the Big Dipper asterism and nearby benchmark systems.

hip-54061.x: Northern pointer star of the Big Dipper bowl; extending a line from Merak through Dubhe points directly to Polaris.

gaia-856096765753549056.x: Southern pointer star of the Big Dipper bowl, an A-type subgiant surrounded by a warm circumstellar debris disk.

hip-58001.x: Main-sequence A-type star forming the lower inner corner of the Big Dipper bowl.
hip-58001.t: Gamma Ursae Majoris · Dipper Bowl Base

gaia-1575287046603605888.x: Faintest of the seven Big Dipper stars, marking the hinge between the bowl and the curving handle.

hip-62956.x: Chemically peculiar Ap star and brightest luminary in Ursa Major, marking the base of the Great Bear’s tail.
hip-62956.t: Epsilon Ursae Majoris · Brightest Bear Star

gaia-1563590579347125632.x: Celebrated multiple star system in the Dipper handle, famously resolved by Benedetto Castelli and Galileo in 1617.

gaia-1565090003967879424.x: Visual companion to Mizar separated by ~12 arcminutes, historically used as an eyesight test across cultures.

hip-67301.x: Young blue-white main-sequence star terminating the handle of the Big Dipper.
hip-67301.t: Eta Ursae Majoris · Tip of the Handle

gaia-762815470562110464.x: Fifth closest stellar system to the Sun (8.31 ly), an active red dwarf hosting multiple confirmed exoplanets.

gaia-777254360337133312.x: Solar analogue (~45.3 ly) hosting a benchmark multi-planet system of Jovian gas giants discovered in the 1990s.

b.s: IAU officially recognized constellations, landmark stellar asterisms, and benchmark member stars.
